status: DRAFT 2026-10-28 - fill S0 inputs, freeze (acceptance.json + sha256) before stage S2; never edit after a production spectrum exists
question: Does AB stacking give ReS2 excitons a permanent out-of-plane dipole (AA forbidden by symmetry), and does it account for the ~13 meV Stark shift?

li.method: G0W0-BSE few-layer AA/AB along and across the Re chain
li.support: van der Laan et al., ACS Photonics 10 (2023), DOI 10.1021/acsphotonics.3c00477

prior_expectation_declared.note: an interlayer shift of ~2.6 A (van der Laan: AB interlayer distance 2.61 A) can give a fraction-of-a-layer e-h offset; 13 meV at F_in ~0.03 V/nm needs d ~0.4 A

definitions.layer_weights: w_e(l), w_h(l) from |A_vck|^2 x layer fraction of |psi_nk|^2; same-gauge WFN + eigenvectors
definitions.F_in: F_ext / eps_perp (eps_perp computed by sawtooth DFT, S1)

G4_magnitude.target: linear part of 13 meV (full 13 meV if not separated)

non_vacuity: G0-G4 can each fail; G2 is a symmetry null, G3 the positive; outcomes recorded before any eigenvector is read
scorers: layer_weights.py (validated on a synthetic two-layer test)

compute.route: 1-2x H100 with dph_total verified; S0-S2 + G1 first (free)
compute.disk_rule: heavy files stay remote; eigenvectors + WFN pulled together or layer weights computed remotely
